chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When one of you loves his Muslim brother, let him ask him about his name, the name of his father, the name of his tribe, and his clan. For it is from his obligatory right and the truthfulness of brotherhood that he asks him about that; otherwise, it is a recognition of foolishness.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a Muslim brother regarding knowing each other's lineage?
ai.summary: In the pre-Islamic and early Islamic context where tribal identity was paramount, this hadith elevates lineage inquiry from mere social courtesy to an obligatory right (haqq) of brotherhood, ensuring deep, authentic connection rather than superficial acquaintance. Scholars note that 'knowledge of foolishness' implies that neglecting this due diligence results in a bond lacking the depth required for true spiritual and social solidarity.
